items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: the agency used to be Tom Archer, and I still think he might be alive or some of his relatives

ctx.x: sometime, and take the uniforms off and get back in the car -- and we haven't checked in anyplace yet. And from Buffalo, the next stop we made was Sioux City, Iowa. Now that's a lot of traveling -- that was two or three days in those days by auto. And I never slept a wink; I was never so thrilled in my life. I was traveling and watching the countryside -- I'd never seen corn and hogs on the way.

Sioux City. Now we worked -- the agency used to be Tom Archer, and I still think he might be alive or some of his relatives -- Tom Archer. He used to hire the territorial bands, and he used to have a whole string of ballrooms, some of them were out in the prairie; Sioux City, Iowa, Sioux Falls, Pipestone, Minnesota and Kansas City, which I'll get to -- we haven't got there yet -- and Lincoln, Nebraska, we had to play in a sandstorm.

This Tom Archer -- his ace in the whole was a six-piece orchestra and was called Lawrence Welk, doing one nighters -- 7 one nighters a week, and they made hundreds and hundreds of thousands of dollars; they were sold out playing polkas, and we would follow them with our appetizing 13 or 14-piece hokum band, they used to call them in those days.
